tasks.label: ПРАВИЛО
tasks.q: Non-defining relative clauses add extra information, use commas and never use that: The captain, whom everyone respects, stays silent. Defining clauses identify the person and have no commas. Reduced relative clauses use participles: the officer refusing the coffee (= who refused), the gun found in the warehouse (= which was found).
tasks.q_pl: Non-defining relative clauses add extra information, use commas and never use that: The captain, whom everyone respects, stays silent. Defining clauses identify the person and have no commas. Reduced relative clauses use participles: the officer refusing the coffee (= who refused), the gun found in the warehouse (= which was found).
tasks.q_en: Non-defining relative clauses add extra information, use commas and never use that: The captain, whom everyone respects, stays silent. Defining clauses identify the person and have no commas. Reduced relative clauses use participles: the officer refusing the coffee (= who refused), the gun found in the warehouse (= which was found).

end_good.title: Місію виконано!
end_good.text: Лісабон підписує звіт, не перечитуючи: «Добре написано». Джейн забирає неторкану чашку й п'є з неї: «Шкода марнувати добру каву». На виході Ріґсбі тихо питає тебе, чи знаєш ти щось про пожежі. «Завтра нас кличуть на підпал. І я там — експерт».
end_good.text_pl: Lisbon podpisuje raport bez czytania: „Dobrze napisane”. Jane zabiera nietknięty kubek i z niego pije: „Szkoda marnować dobrą kawę”. Przy wyjściu Rigsby cicho pyta cię, czy znasz się na pożarach. „Jutro wzywają nas do podpalenia. A ja tam jestem ekspertem”.
end_good.text_en: Lisbon signs the report without rereading it: “Well written.” Jane takes the untouched cup and drinks from it: “Shame to waste good coffee.” On the way out Rigsby quietly asks if you know anything about fires. “Tomorrow we're called to an arson case. And I'm the expert there.”
